newsitem.title: SPAIN: Eight injured in pro-ETA demonstration in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Eight injured in pro-ETA demonstration in Spain.

text.p: At least eight people were injured in a clash between police and supporters of the separatist group ETA on Saturday in the Basque country.

The demonstration in Bilbao was led by Herri Batasuna (HB), the political arm of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), to protest at the arrests this month of some of HB's leaders who failed to respond to a Supreme Court summons.
Two of the demonstrators were in serious condition, hospital sources said. Police, who fired rubber bullets during the protest according to local media, were also hurt in the confrontations.
Tensions have been running high in the northern Basque region after the government blamed ETA for a spate of deadly attacks across the country this week.
The Supreme Court has summoned the 25-member leadership of HB to appear in court and answer charges of distributing a pro-ETA video during last year's election campaign.
Eleven of the leaders who failed to appear were arrested and jailed after refusing to post bail. Three others are in Brussels.
The 11 remaining HB leaders led thousands behind a large banner that read "Democracy for the Basque people''.

Local media reported the demonstrators shouted pro-ETA slogans, hurled insults at police and called for independence for the Basque country. Masked demonstrators spray-painted slogans in favour of the radical Basque rebels.
Police tried to break up the demonstration with force and fired rubber bullets, the reports said.

Earlier this week, the government said ETA was behind the assassination of a Supreme Court Judge in Madrid on Monday and a car bomb hours earlier in the southern city of Granada which killed a hairdresser employed at a military base.
On Tuesday, a Basque businessman was fatally shot in the head during a carnival celebration in the Basque region and ETA was blamed.
The government ordered heightened police presence on the streets after the killings as well as more security for potential targets such as judges, military, police and politicians.
